claimed: mkinney (Claude agent, M5) · 2026-11-10 01:42 UTC · branch issue/616-smoothing (fork synced at v0.16.0) · plan: below

Thanks @spikeypineapple, this is a good one. Here is the design. Comments are welcome before code lands, especially on the roughing/finishing mapping.

**1. What the op says (dialect-neutral):** each operation's section carries a new stream record, `SMOOTH <tol_mm> <finish|rough>`:
- **Finish-type ops** (contour finish, 3D finishing, scallop/parallel finish, and so on) state their own **tolerance**, marked `finish`, so the control is asked for maximum accuracy.
- **Roughing ops** state a tolerance **derived from stock-to-leave**, marked `rough`: a fraction of the stock left, clamped to a sane band. That's your idea: more stock left gives more aggressive smoothing. The exact fraction and band will be a recorded decision; the starting point is tol = stock_to_leave / 5, clamped to 0.01–0.25 mm.
- **Drilling, tapping and probing** state nothing (no smoothing change).

**2. What each post writes** (from each control's public programming documentation):

| Dialect | Smoothing on | Off / reset |
|---|---|---|
| Tormach / LinuxCNC | `G64 P<tol>` (replaces today's fixed header `G64 P0.001`) | `G61` only if asked |
| Fanuc | `G5.1 Q1 R<level>` (AI contour control, level 1-10: finish leads to 1, rough leads up to 10 from the tolerance) | `G5.1 Q0` at section end |
| Haas | `G187 P<1\|2\|3> E<tol>` (P1 rough, P3 finish) | `G187` (reset to default) |
| Sinumerik | `CYCLE832(<tol>, _FINISH\|_ROUGH)` | `CYCLE832()` |
| Heidenhain | `CYCL DEF 32 TOLERANCE` `T<tol>` | (tolerance cycle reset) |
| Mazak | (to be confirmed from its manual; a comment only until then, never a guess) | |

- **Fanuc option:** `G5.1` needs the AI contour option and its R range varies by control version, as you say. So the Fanuc-family posts get a post property, **`Smoothing: off / G5.1`**, defaulting to off, so a control without the option never sees it. The others default on, since their words are standard.
- **Scope:** smoothing is set per operation section, and every post resets it at the section end, so a tolerance never leaks into the next op.

**3. Tests:** a golden per dialect for one finish op and one rough op. A finish op gets the tight word, a rough op with 0.5 mm stock gets the aggressive word, and drilling gets none. The default Fanuc output stays byte-identical.

#614 (the Doosan DNM post) would use the Fanuc `G5.1` mapping above.

fix on mkinney:issue/616-smoothing · PR #635 · pinned by tests/smoothing.rs (4) · merges at the next cut (feat). @spikeypineapple - the option is off by default; if you can try it on a control with smoothing, the Fanuc `G5.1 Q1` / Haas `G187` / Siemens `CYCLE832` output is the part we could only check against documentation.
